chunks: And the major sins are forbidden

namely: associating partners with Allah, the Exalted; killing the soul which Allah has forbidden; disrespecting parents; fleeing from the ranks in battle; devouring the property of an orphan oppressively; consuming usury after clear proof; falsely accusing chaste women; and after that, adultery, sodomy, and theft; eating dead animals, blood, and pork, and what is offered to other than Allah without necessity; consuming ill-gotten wealth; shortchanging in measure and weight; gambling; false testimony; losing hope in Allah's spirit (/forgiveness); feeling secure from Allah's plot; despairing of Allah's mercy; abandoning helping the oppressed and leaning towards the tyrants; the false oath that drowns (in sin); withholding rights without hardship; using haughtiness, arrogance, lying, extravagance, and wastefulness; treachery; underestimating the Hajj; fighting the friends of Allah, the Exalted; and entertainments that divert from the remembrance of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, such as singing and playing strings, are disliked, as is persisting in minor sins.
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in this is sufficient for a people of worshippers.'

The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'The major sins are seven, and after them [others]. So every sin is major in relation to what is smaller than it, and minor in relation to what is greater than it. This is the meaning of what As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) mentioned in this hadith regarding the major sins exceeding the seven, and there is no power except with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the major sins (Kaba'ir) listed in Shia hadith and how are they defined?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq expands the traditional seven major sins by enumerating a broader spectrum of grave transgressions, including specific sins like fleeing battle and consuming *suh* (unjust wealth), while emphasizing the relativity of sin magnitude. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking legal prohibitions with spiritual states, such as despair (*qanoot*) and arrogance (*takabbur*), to provide a comprehensive guide for the devout. The compiler’s note underscores that 'major' and 'minor' are contextual, reinforcing the idea that persistence in small sins can elevate them to major status.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-15 “And the major sins are as follows: associating partners with the Honorable the Exalted God; murdering someone which is prohibited by the Honorable the Exalted God; disrespecting parents’ rights; fleeing from holy war; oppressively devouring an orphan’s property; taking usury after knowing its unlawfulness; unduly ascribing adultery to chaste women; committing adultery; sodomizing; stealing; eating flesh of dead animals; drinking blood; eating pork; eating what has been offered for anyone other than God; eating ill-gotten property; selling underweight goods; gambling; falsely testifying; losing hope in God’s Forgiveness; feeling secure from God’s Plots; abandoning helping of the oppressed; relying on oppressors; false swearing; blocking (people’s due) rights; Haughtiness; oppressing one’s inferiors; telling lies; wastefulness; overspending; treachery; underestimating the Hajj pilgrimage; fighting with the friends of the Honorable the Exalted God. Moreover engaging in whatever would keep one far from God’s remembrance such as singing or playing musical instruments and persisting in doing minor sins is admonished against.”
Then As-Sadiq (MGB) added, “This is sufficient for the servants who are obedient.”

The compiler of the book added, “There are seven absolutely major sins. However, the sins mentioned thereafter are more major than minor sins, and are less severe than the major sins. This is what As-Sadiq (MGB) intended to say by naming more than seven major sins here. There is no power save in God.”
